title: Methods and diagnostics for spin liquids
intro: ED, DMRG, partons/VMC, NQS, thermodynamics, parallel computing

questions.question: Why can't ARPACK reliably count a 4-fold topological degeneracy with a tiny Krylov space?
options: Lanczos generates a single vector per degenerate eigenspace from one start vector; restarts or a large Krylov space are needed
questions.explanation: qslab uses ncv >= 40; symmetry operators then label the sectors.

questions.question: Which quantity distinguishes a gapped Z2 spin liquid from a trivial paramagnet?
questions.explanation: Area law S = alpha L - gamma; only topological order has gamma > 0.

questions.question: A smoking gun for fractionalisation in neutron scattering is
options: a broad continuum in S(q, w) instead of sharp magnons
questions.explanation: Spinons are created in pairs, so the two-particle states form a continuum.

questions.question: The QMC sign problem prevents
options: unbiased QMC for frustrated Heisenberg models
questions.explanation: The Kitaev model is sign-free in the Majorana representation, so Majorana MC is exact up to statistics.

questions.question: In qslab FTLM, independent random vectors are distributed over
options: threads or MPI ranks via pmap
questions.explanation: Embarrassingly parallel: R random vectors and all Sz sectors.

questions.question: Which parallel strategy suits a single huge ED matrix-vector product on one node?
options: shared-memory Numba 'pull' kernel (each thread owns output rows)
questions.explanation: The pull formulation needs no atomics; scipy CSR matvec is single-threaded.

questions.question: How many parameters does an RBM with alpha = 2 have for N = 16 spins?
DMRG entanglement on a cylinder of width W grows as
options: S ~ W (area law), so chi ~ exp(W)
questions.explanation: That is why 2D DMRG is limited to W of about 10-12.
